turns.content: Let d and e be the integer common differences of the arithmetic sequences (a_j) and (b_j). Express a_14 and b_20 in terms of a_20, b_14, d, and e.
Use a_20+b_14=1000 to show that b_20+a_14=1000+6(e-d), and identify its congruence class modulo 6.
Determine the smallest positive integer in that congruence class and prove that it is impossible when all forty terms are distinct positive integers and d,e are nonzero integers.
Find the next positive integer in the same congruence class and state the resulting lower bound, without assuming yet that it is attainable.
Build an attainment witness by taking a_j=23-j and b_20=1. Use the required cross-sum to derive the common difference and initial term of (b_j), then state both sequence formulas.
For the two formulas just obtained, compute a_20,b_14,b_20,a_14 and verify both required cross-sums without changing the construction.
List the ranges and discrete term formulas of the two sequences and verify positivity within each sequence.
Prove cross-sequence disjointness exactly; do not infer intersection merely from overlap of continuous numerical ranges. Conclude whether all forty terms are distinct.
Combine the lower bound and valid construction to give the least possible value of b_20+a_14.
